title: Atlas of Hegemony 1492–2010
metaDesc: An interactive world map of 16 moments from 1492 to 2010, layering the struggle for hegemony, who gained and lost from key events, and developments in technology and ideas.
subtitle: Over each year's borders: the struggle for hegemony · gains and losses · technology · ideas
hint: Colours show who ruled at that time, and each country has its own fixed colour. The stronger the colour, the firmer the rule; hatching means rule that is weakening or contested; a very pale colour means the country has left the contest for hegemony but still exists. Tap an area for its name and source; tap a country in the list below to keep only that country and follow its course and territory over time. ◆ marks strategic points such as straits, canals and bases; where the source map was wrong, the map has been recoloured with checked values.
footHtml: Borders: up to 1880, historical-basemaps (André Ourednik et al., GPL-3.0) with year-by-year corrections; from 1914, redrawn from CShapes 2.0 (Schvitz, Girardin, Weidmann et al., dated borders and colonies). For 1914 onwards, where both sources exist, the ‘Cross-check’ section of each year shows the agreement rate and where they differ. Strategic points and some regions were recoloured with checked values where the source was wrong. Territory areas are approximations computed by sampling the final map on a 0.25° grid. Because the gaps between years are uneven, ‘Gains and losses’ covers the main events since the previous year shown.

ui.ckAbsentLong: The source border data does not draw this point (a small island or base). This marker is the checked value.
ui.ckDiffLong: ⚠ This differs from the map colour. The source border data draws this point as {map}. Small places such as bases and straits get swallowed by the surrounding area, or the source label is wrong — this marker is the checked value.
ui.ckMapNone: an area it does not draw
ui.trackAllNote: What has changed since the previous year shown. Tap a country to see its whole course.
ui.trackNote: Tap a year to go to that map.
ui.trackBefore: Not treated as a contender on this map before {year}
ui.regionName: Name of the area at the time
ui.ckPatchedLong: In the source map this point was swallowed by the surrounding area or wrongly labelled, so the map itself has been recoloured with the checked ruler.
ui.vCs: Borders at this point were redrawn from CShapes 2.0 (as of {date}). Agreement with the open-source map used before (historical-basemaps): {agree}% (by area, 0.25° grid sample, coastline differences excluded). Strategic points and regions recoloured: {p}.
ui.vHb: Before 1886 there is no dated dataset to cross-check against. Based on historical-basemaps, {f} sovereignty-label errors were corrected and {p} strategic points and regions recoloured with checked values.
ui.vDiffs: Where the two sources differ most (source ↔ CShapes)
ui.vAdopt: Where they differ, the map follows CShapes.
ui.vExc: Shown differently from CShapes, or with a note added
ui.sparkNote: Areas are recomputed from what is coloured on this map (colonies included). Before 1886 they include nominal claims and spheres, so they can exceed real control.
ui.colorKeyNote: A country keeps the same colour even when its name changes (Russia → USSR → Russia, Ming → Qing → China). When it grows stronger or weaker, the colour stays and only its strength and hatching change.
